items.title: Omarchy runs on the new M5 Max MacBook Pro: GPU, touch screen and WiFi working
items.summary: A builder got the Omarchy Linux desktop running on Apple's new M5 Max MacBook Pro with the GPU, touch screen and WiFi working, and published a write-up with the needed PRs so an agent can replicate it. The Neural Engine powers up; some polish is left.

items.title: Mac Studio 512GB versus four ASUS GX10 boxes serving DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, same benchmark
items.summary: A side-by-side of one 512GB Mac Studio (mlx-serve) and four 128GB GX10 Spark-class machines (spark-ds41f recipe) on the original DeepSeek V4.1 Flash weights: 53/84 vs 73/122 tok/s at one user, 137/148 vs 330/847 tok/s at 16 users, and 128K prefill 3,325 vs 7,522 tok/s, at similar prices.
items.vendor: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash on Mac Studio vs ASUS GX10

doubt.pushback: Single third-party run with no repo or script linked for the benchmark, so the numbers cannot be reproduced from the post.

items.title: vLLM adds NVIDIA Canary speech recognition and translation, plus Parakeet TDT and Nemotron diarization plugins
items.summary: A contributor landed PRs that let vLLM serve NVIDIA Canary (speech recognition and translation to and from English in 25 European languages, token-identical to the reference), Parakeet TDT and Nemotron-3-Diarization via plugins, and GPU-side image normalization for Gemma 4.

items.title: LiteLLM adds performance alerts for spend spikes, traffic spikes, error rates and latency
items.summary: LiteLLM now flags spend spikes, traffic spikes, higher error rates and slower responses across teams, users, keys and models. Docs blog post is linked.
